source_review.notes: Checked all 12 structured references against official NIST, HHS, EUR-Lex, UK ICO, Google Cloud and primary/publisher research sources. Verified de-identification governance and release models, HIPAA-specific Expert Determination/Safe Harbor framing, GDPR pseudonymization and identifiability context, current ICO guidance, format-preserving encryption scope, current masking/tokenization transformations, k-anonymity, and foundational differential-privacy definitions. HHS and the k-anonymity publisher rejected command-line retrieval with bot-protection responses but were independently accessible through indexed official/publisher pages; EUR-Lex returned accepted status 202; the remaining final URLs returned HTTP 200.

evidence: Checked symbols for input/output generations, transforms and parameters, use, recipient/environment, adversary, release history, risk/utility thresholds, quasi-identifier equivalence classes and disclosure-risk dimensions.

Checked k-anonymity minimum, differential-privacy probability inequality, adjacency, epsilon/delta, deterministic-token equality/domain notation and all GitHub math delimiters for defined symbols and balanced syntax.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently separates contextual risk/utility decisions, equivalence-class properties, randomized privacy guarantees and deterministic linkage behavior.

evidence: Executed equivalence-class-boundary and matched four records, one generalized class, minimum class size and k equal to four, minimum sensitive diversity one, and both stated Boolean conclusions exactly.
Recomputed all generalized keys: ages 29/31/34/36 map to 20-39 and postal codes 02139/02138/02140/02141 map to 021, while all conditions remain rare.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic fixture correctly demonstrates k=4 alongside homogeneous sensitive-attribute disclosure without representing real subjects.

evidence: Verified the k-anonymity definition as minimum equivalence-class cardinality for a declared quasi-identifier projection.
Verified the homogeneous-class construction satisfies k-anonymity for k or more rows while revealing the common sensitive value conditional on class membership.

Verified the differential-privacy inequality is explicitly conditional on adjacency, mechanism parameters and outputs, and deterministic-token equality is presented as preserved linkage rather than anonymity.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Formal claims state distinct guarantees and do not infer attribute confidentiality or universal anonymity from k, masking, tokenization or noise.

evidence: Reviewed empty releases, rare/unique rows, homogeneous sensitive values, high-dimensional sparsity, nulls, free text/media, precise space/time, background knowledge, overlapping releases, small cells, differencing and reconstruction.

Reviewed plain hashes, salts, deterministic equality, domain reuse, chosen-input oracles, token collisions/truncation, vault/key compromise, retries, rotation, backups, recovery, deletion and mixed-token joins.

Reviewed partial transformations, raw logs/dead letters/intermediates, alternate paths, synthetic memorization, subgroup bias, differential-privacy contribution/adjacency/composition failures, public irreversibility and changing auxiliary data.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial review covers identity, attribute, membership, linkage, inference, reconstruction, cryptographic, operational, utility, composition and lifecycle boundaries.

evidence: Traced exact input/output generation, goal, recipient/environment, protected unit, threat/auxiliary knowledge, release history, transform/code/config/key/domain, coverage, risk, utility, review and validity through exposition, examples and answers.

Confirmed raw inputs, mappings, keys, intermediates, failures and logs remain protected; eligible/transformed/failed scope reconciles; and outputs receive lineage, owner, classification, access, retention and expiry.
Confirmed masking, tokenization, encryption, pseudonymization, k-anonymity, differential privacy, synthesis and legal determinations remain distinct with explicit assumptions and residual risk.
invariant_checking.notes: No transform name, detector result, sample test, class-size statistic, noisy output, synthetic label, successful attack or failed attack is described as broader proof than it supplies.

evidence: Reviewed the construction of at least k records with identical released quasi-identifiers and one common sensitive value.
Confirmed the class satisfies the stated equivalence-class cardinality while class-membership knowledge reveals the sensitive attribute without row identification.
Confirmed the conclusion is limited to insufficiency of k-anonymity alone and does not claim every k-anonymous release is unsafe or every diversity extension sufficient.
proof_review.notes: The counterexample validly separates identity ambiguity under Q from sensitive-attribute confidentiality.

evidence: The k-anonymity insufficiency argument is explicitly labeled Claim and Proof rather than empirical evidence.
The following limitation bounds the construction and distinguishes it from universal safety conclusions.
The executable is explicitly described as a fixture illustration rather than real-person data or certification.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Definition, proof, deterministic recomputation, contextual risk assessment, implementation control and legal determination are labeled distinctly.

evidence: Current regulatory guidance, standards and product transformation behavior is attributed to dated official or primary sources in its stated jurisdiction/product scope.
Risk attacks, coverage reconciliation, key/vault evidence, utility measurements, recipient conditions and release-history checks are framed as scoped evidence with limitations.
The chapter explicitly rejects deriving legal anonymity, compliance, future attack resistance or every-recipient safety from a tool, transform, metric or absence of a successful attack.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Normative definitions, current implementation behavior, mathematical guarantees, deterministic fixtures, empirical attacks/metrics and qualified legal decisions remain separate.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the chapter end to end. It integrates release/threat modeling, masking, suppression, token architectures, hashing/encryption boundaries, quasi-identifier transformations, k-anonymity limits, aggregate composition, differential privacy, synthesis, unstructured modalities, risk/utility evaluation, protected pipelines and time-bounded governance without presenting any technique as universal anonymity.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed the release record, falsifiable claim, domain-separated token/vault/key design, collision/oracle/retry/rotation behavior, full-scope transformation pipeline, protected intermediates and failures, output registration, risk attacks, utility checks, release review, monitoring, partner controls and compromised-key incident answer for production usability.

pedagogical_review.notes: Reviewed progression from the one-page contextual model through prerequisites, release models, masking, tokenization, quasi-identifiers, aggregates, differential privacy, synthesis, pipeline, lifecycle, notation, formal counterexample, executable, 12 trade-offs, 30 misconceptions, ten distinct examples, connections and five exercises with complete answers. Connections accurately retrieve DE-028/066/076/078/082/084-086 and prepare DE-088.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
